The security context depends on the intended use and application and includes, but is not limited to:
—    Protection of the perimeters of the security context, if applicable;

—    all countermeasures concerning the interaction between different functional units inside the security
context;

—    all countermeasures to be applied within the security context.

The countermeasures provided by security context are effective as long as assumptions of the following kind
are documented and fulfilled:
a)   physical and logical access management for the target users,

b)   intended use and foreseeable misuse.

c)   physical environment including compensating countermeasure,

d)   logical environment including compensating countermeasure,

e)   policies and procedures,

NOTE       “Security context” is the security equivalent of “intended use” in the safety domain.




      32

                                                                                            prEN 50742:2025 (E)



The following are examples (not comprehensive list) and consideration of the assumptions related to the
countermeasures provided by security context.
a)   physical and logical access management for the target users

— everybody

— authorized personnel

— service technician

b)   intended use and foreseeable misuse

— use remote diagnostic connection permanently to supervise

c)   Physical environment including compensating countermeasure

— location

— outdoors: agriculture, forest, construction sites, …

— public buildings, hospitals, schools …

— public transportation, airports, trains, …

— premises with access restrictions (access only allowed to people with a badge and authentication
etc.): Industrial facilities, logistic hubs, warehouses, …

— special restrictions

— locked cabinets

—    distinguish between locks with generic keys and unique keys.

— inside a machine’s housing

— physical position

— static

— mobile

— autonomously moving around

d)   logical environment including compensating countermeasure

— allow only access via VPN?

— continuous connection or on demand only

— is some type of a firewall required if connected to a untrusted network?

— list all network connections, direct or indirect, logical and physical

— how is the network supposed to be installed (access to cables, communication partners, etc.)

e)   policies and procedures.



                                                                                                              33

      prEN 50742:2025 (E)



— e.g. enforce certain complexity and length for passwords.

After considering all assumptions, you can estimate an attacker capability score according to Table B.2 and
Table B.3 in Annex B for “Window of Opportunity” for a successful attack

—    This machine is supposed to be used inside an industrial facility with standard access control, so only
authenticated and authorized personnel is allowed to near the machine.

—    The PLC is housed inside a locked cabinet with a unique key, which is handed to authorized personnel
only. (EL0 according to Annex B)

—    The network cables between motor drive and safety PLC are inside the machine and not accessible from
the outside without disassembling the machine. (EL0 according to Annex B)

—    Connection to the configuration interfaces is established only intermittently, only for service cases and
trouble shooting.

— For a direct connection (Ethernet or USB) between a PC and the PLC, EL1 can be assumed.

— The USB interface that allows for configuration of the PLC is connected to the edge of the cabinet
via a extension cable and thus can be accessed by people with physical access,
elevating the Exposure level from EL0 to EL1 according to Annex B

— The remote configuration connection is used only with a direct Ethernet cable or via a secured means
of remote access (e.g. a VPN)

— The secured remote access connection is left unpowered if no connection is needed (reducing the
“Window of Opportunity”)

— If remote access is desired, the Exposure Level might be for example EL4.

— Then the secured remote access connection needs to provide measures to reduce the risk from
EL4 with adequate measures as laid out in 5.4.

—    Connection to the standard PLC is kept up permanently for diagnosis and standard control activities

—    The memory device holding the safety configuration is placed inside the PLC inside the locked cabinet

—    The loader crane is typically used outdoors in public accessible areas without physical access controls.

—    The remote control unit for the crane can be used outdoors.

—    The receiver unit is inside a locked box.

—    If the crane is not in use, the wireless control system is not powered.

—    If the crane is used, the operator has to see the arm.

attributes.clauseText:
Trust Boundaries identify areas at a similar level of trust and isolate them from other areas at a different level of
trust. This applies to physical and logical properties. This is normally part of the data flow diagram, however it
can be considered a separate step as well.
The intention of grouping assets into zones and conduits is to identify those assets which share common security
requirements and to permit the identification of common security measures required to mitigate risk.
NOTE       The data flow diagram usually includes the trust boundaries of the system under consideration.




      38

                                                                                                  prEN 50742:2025 (E)




869

Figure C.9

NOTE

Boundary: edge

Zone: area inside a boundary

Practical examples consider, several different trust boundaries. Those trust boundaries correspond with the
different attack surfaces and can be labelled with the “Exposure Levels” defined in Annex B.
The examples show how to regard the system elements from the most trusted areas to the most exposed ones.

This example considers everything inside the machine as a fully trusted environment, because it requires some
sort of authentication to access, e.g. a unique key or a special tool to open the machine, or some sort of software
authentication.
Components attached to the outside of the machine like a local HMI, the USB configuration interface of the
Safety PLC, and actuators are considered in the “physical access” category.
The Ethernet connection is intended to be used with local devices, such as fieldbus sensors and actuators or
other PLCs (thus “local access” exposure zone).
The industrial factory network contains access by engineering tools and other machines etc.
If the security context section in the information of use describes e.g. that the fieldbus connection is designed
to be used locally only, then compensating countermeasures are necessary to use the system in the intended
manner. This example mandates a network transition device (like a smart switch, a router with integrated firewall
etc.) to keep it separated from more exposure than allowed.
The same is true for other trust boundaries. As in our example the user shall be able to access the application
remotely, the remote access shall be secured by an external measure such as a firewall or a secure
communication end point to keep the adjacent level separated from the unrestricted level.

Answer the question: “Where can corruption cause adverse effects (directly or indirectly) on the risk reduction
measures (according to EN ISO 12100:2010)?”.
Consider attacks on all elements in your data flow diagram.
How can the interfaces or protocols be misused considering the defined assumptions?
You should use appropriate tools and techniques such as STRIDE for such a consideration.
Control system consists of INPUT – LOGIC – OUTPUT.
Our STRIDE analysis encompasses the whole system, including:
—    the control system consisting of INPUT – LOGIC – OUTPUT,

—    system interfaces,



      42

                                                                                                prEN 50742:2025 (E)



—   configuration of devices,

—   actual operation of the devices.

Chain of trust concept: If data flows happen in a trusted boundary only, there
Spoofing – “impersonate a valid system user or resource” REF1 – violating authentication
—   Spoof another safety communication peer data, e.g. by faking stuffing scheme, time stamps, counters,
CRCs etc. between controllers, impersonating safety controllers

—   Replay attacks, simulating valid sensor data on a fieldbus

—   An attacker logs into a configuration interface as an administrator to modify safety configuration

Tampering – “Modifying system or user data” REF1 – violating integrity
—   Somebody modifies safety related parameters, configuration, firmware, or user software

—   Somebody performs a man-in-the-middle attack to modify process data while faking safety protocol’s
measures against communication errors

—   Somebody simulates/bypasses a safety input device, such as an E-Stop. The real E-Stop events are not
detected/evaluated correctly anymore.

Repudiation – “performing an illegal operation and denying involvement.”– violating accountability
—   Somebody deletes or modifies log entries related to modification of safety related parameters,
configuration, firmware, or user software

Information Disclosure – “expose information to individuals who are not supposed to see it” REF1 – violating
confidentiality
—   Probably not in scope as long as health and safety properties of the machine or related product remain
unchanged

Denial of Service – “Making the system temporarily unavailable or unusable” REF1 – violating availability
—   Probably not in scope as long as health and safety properties of the machine or related product remain
unchanged

Elevation of Privileges – “unprivileged user gains privileged access” REF1 – violating authorization
—   Probably not in scope as long as health and safety properties of the machine or related product remain
unchanged.

List of threats and mitigations

Threats should be countered primarily by countermeasures by this annex and if that is not practically reasonable,
compensating countermeasures should be considered.
Mitigations can either have an effect on
—    the impact of the attack,

—    or disrupt the attack path.

Goal should be a catalogue of possible mitigations, e.g.
—    input validation,

—    least privilege principle,

—    secure defaults,

—    kerckhoff principle, security should hinge on a well-defined secret, not on obscure design,

—    immutable application code,

—    separate memory for execution and data,

—    read-only memory,

—    etc.

Bonus if all of these mitigations get test criteria to make them verifiable.

4 General considerations
The cybersecurity process described in this document is from the perspective of a product during all phases
of the product’s lifecycle to ensure an appropriate level of security.
A product consists of various components (e.g. the engine, wheels, and ECUs). Together all components are
used to fulfil the functions of a product (e.g. Driving and Remote Data Processing). In Figure 1, the product
(e.g. a tractor) consists of two functions (Function: Driving and Function: Remote Data Processing). The
Function: Driving contains the components wheel, engine, gearbox, Engine Control Unit and Transmission
Control Unit. The Function: Remote Data Processing contains the Telemetry Unit. The manufacturer (OEM)
defines the system of interest as shown in Figure 1 including the Engine Control Unit, Transmission Control
Unit, Telemetry Unit and messages between the ECUs.

The product and the corresponding system of interest may vary between the OEM and a supplier. For a
supplier, the product may be a single ECU which will be part of an overall OEM product function (e.g.
Function: Driving) as shown in Figure 2. The supplier defines the system of interest as shown in Figure 2
including only the Telematics Unit and messages between the ECUs.

the decision diagram shown in Figure 3. If the candidate system of interest is determined to be cybersecurity
relevant, then the risk assessment process defined in clause 5 shall be applied. Clause 5 describes the risk
assessment process in detail and covers the requirements and work packages for asset identification, impact
rating, threat scenario identification, risk rating and risk treatment decision.

The vulnerability and incident handling processes specified in Clause 8 shall be applied as a means to define
the appropriate activities in case a weakness is identified in a system of interest.

5 Risk assessment for the system of interest
attributes.clauseTitle: includes examples of roles that can exist in an organisation.

attributes.clauseText:
The system of interest shall have a risk assessment performed and risk treatments shall be identified
per clause 5. The risk assessment may be performed at different levels of a machine. For example, a risk
assessment may be done at the highest level of the machine considering the whole machine and external
interfaces. At a lower level, a risk assessment may be done on a sub-system of the machine such as steering
system, power train system, functional component, etc. For a product, all cybersecurity relevant sub-
systems shall be evaluated. Reference Annex A to understand the roles that should be included in a risk
assessment.
The risk assessment typically includes the work products and sequence flow as shown in Figure 5.




                                                              ﻿
                                             © ISO 2025 – All rights reserved
                                                             8

                                Licensed to Inlab / Simone Fornaciari (s.fornaciari@inlab.srl)
                             ISO Store Order: OP-1037245 license #1/ Downloaded: 2026-03-26
                                Single user licence only, copying and networking prohibited.
                                           ISO/DIS 24882:2025(en)




                             Figure 5 — Risk assessment sequence diagram

For the risk assessment, identify and document the boundary of the system of interest, including the
components, interfaces, functions, and architectures that are within the boundary.

The following information shall be identified and documented for the system of interest:
a)   A boundary diagram or description to identify the interfaces/data and to clarify what elements are part
     of the system being analysed.
b) A functional diagram or description to identify the intended purpose of the system of interest.
c)   A data flow diagram or description to identify the cybersecurity relevant data flow.
Items a) through c) above shall include the following details:
— List of diagnostic services that can be used to access/manipulate internal data (if exists);


                                                             ﻿
                                            © ISO 2025 – All rights reserved
                                                            9

                                  Licensed to Inlab / Simone Fornaciari (s.fornaciari@inlab.srl)
                               ISO Store Order: OP-1037245 license #1/ Downloaded: 2026-03-26
                                  Single user licence only, copying and networking prohibited.
                                             ISO/DIS 24882:2025(en)

— List of assets that include/embed/contribute to any functional safety control (if exists);
— List of assets that include/embed/contribute to any function the absence of which can have negative
  satisfaction to user (if exists).

Identify the assets and damage scenarios within the system of interest that may require cybersecurity
protection.

The damage scenario shall be identified. The list of damage scenarios should include:
— items such as, but not limited to, interrupting core product functions or essential services, stealing,
  manipulating, depriving, or deleting personal or other data / software; and
— at least the impact categories safety, financial, privacy, and availability for the user.
The manufacturer shall identify the asset(s) that can be the target of an attack to realize any identified
damage scenario.
Each identified asset shall be assigned one or more cybersecurity properties (e.g. confidentiality, integrity,
availability). Additional specific properties can be used (e.g. authorization, authenticity, non-repudiation,
freshness).
NOTE 1    A pre-defined list (e.g. damage scenarios, assets) can be created, maintained, and updated periodically by
the manufacturer.

NOTE 2    Asset list can include items such as:

—   Any data flow from an external connection interface that can be exploited to lead to a damage scenario;

—   Any commands, calibration, settings, configuration data which rest in the system of interest or is in transit to or
    from the system of interest that, if manipulated, can lead to a damage scenario;

—   Any personal data at rest or in transit to the system of interest;

—   Any hardware or software components related to core product functionality and safety of the system of interest.

                                 Licensed to Inlab / Simone Fornaciari (s.fornaciari@inlab.srl)
                              ISO Store Order: OP-1037245 license #1/ Downloaded: 2026-03-26
                                 Single user licence only, copying and networking prohibited.
                                            ISO/DIS 24882:2025(en)

Refer to Annex B for damage scenario examples which can be considered for the impact categories: safety,
financial, privacy, and availability.
Identify the threat scenarios within the system of interest.

Threats shall be identified that can compromise the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of an identified
asset to realize an identified damage scenario.
The threat identification method can align to various modelling methods such as[5] STRIDE[6], VAST[7],
PASTA, etc.
The identification activity shall include the evaluation of accidental corruption that can lead to a damage
scenario.
NOTE 1    The threats considered can include but are not limited to:

—   unauthorized access;

—   tampering;

—   data breaches;

—   denial of service;

—   misuse (implies intentional);

—   misconfiguration (implies unintentional).

NOTE 2    A pre-defined list (e.g. threats scenarios, damage scenarios, assets) can be created, maintained, and
updated periodically by the manufacturer.

                                             © ISO 2025 – All rights reserved

                                 ISO Store Order: OP-1037245 license #1/ Downloaded: 2026-03-26
                                    Single user licence only, copying and networking prohibited.
                                               ISO/DIS 24882:2025(en)

NOTE 3     A threat scenario can lead to multiple damage scenarios and a damage scenario can correspond to multiple
threat scenarios.

The work products of clause 5.4 shall include:
— [WP-5.4-01] List of threat scenarios;
— [WP-5.4-02] Mapping of assets to threat scenarios and damage scenarios.
NOTE      [WP-5.4-02] is a superset of [WP-5.3-03] and can be created in one document by extending [WP-5.3-03]
with the mapping of damage scenarios to threat scenarios.

The damage scenarios will be evaluated and assigned to an impact rating. The impact rating is required to
determine the overall risk rating. Risk rating is based on the impact rating and the likelihood rating.

The following work product shall be available:
— List of damage scenarios [WP-5.3-02].

The impact rating for each of the four impact categories (safety, financial, privacy, and availability) shall be
determined for each damage scenario using Table 1, Table 2, Table 3, and Table 4.
In the impact tables (Table 1, Table 2, Table 3, and Table 4), the assessor shall consider the users to be the
owner, operator, or bystander.
The maximum impact for each of the four impact categories (safety, financial, privacy, and availability) shall
be determined for the risk assessment. The categories with lower impact rating may be omitted.
EXAMPLE 1       Given the impact rating for the categories Safety: “Major”, Financial: “Moderate”, Privacy: “Negligible”,
Availability: “Negligible” will result in an overall rating of “Major”.

EXAMPLE 2       Given the impact rating for the categories Safety: “Negligible”, Financial: “Severe”, Privacy: “Negligible”,
Availability: “Negligible” will result in an overall rating of “Severe”.

Personal data can be defined in accordance with[9] ISO/IEC 29100:2024 for Table 3.

                                       Table 1 — Safety impact rating criteria
Impact Rating            Criteria for safety impact rating
Severe                   Life-threatening injuries (survival uncertain), severe disability
Major                    Severe and life-threatening injuries (survival probable), permanent partial loss in work capacity
Moderate                 Light and moderate injuries, requires medical attention, total recovery
Negligible               No injuries, damage limited to property
NOTE 1 This table aligns with definitions from[3] EN ISO 25119-1:2023 & A1:2023. Controllability and exposure in accordance
with[8] EN ISO 25119-2:2023 can also be considered for rating impact on safety, if a rational is provided.
NOTE 2 For earth-moving or construction machinery, the criteria descriptions of this table may be replaced by[4] ISO 19014-1:2018
criteria. Controllability and exposure in accordance with[4] ISO 19014-1:2018 can also be considered for rating impact on safety,
if a rational is provided.

Moderate                 Financial damage leads to inconvenient consequences which the affected user will be able to

NOTE The assessor can also consider the financial impact to the manufacturer in addition to the impact to the user.

Impact Rating            Criteria for privacy impact rating

                         Information regarding the user is easy to link to personal data and/or requires very high pro-

                         I

The work products of clause 5.5 shall include:
— [WP-5.5-01] List of assigned impact ratings for each damage scenario.

Determine the likelihood rating for each threat scenario. The likelihood rating is required to determine the
overall risk rating. Risk rating is based on the impact rating and the likelihood rating.

                                                                    ﻿
                                                   © ISO 2025 – All rights reserved

                                ISO Store Order: OP-1037245 license #1/ Downloaded: 2026-03-26
                                   Single user licence only, copying and networking prohibited.
                                              ISO/DIS 24882:2025(en)

For each threat scenario, determine the numeric value for each of the subcategories (i.e. elapsed time,
specialist expertise, knowledge of system of interest, window of opportunity, equipment) by identifying the
applicable level for each column in Table 5.
Each column of Table 5 is explained in Table 6 through Table 9.

              Table 5 — Subcategories to determine the likelihood value for a threat scenario
                                             Knowledge of                     Window of Opportu-
Elapsed Time        Specialist Expertise                                                            Equipment
                                             System of Interest               nity
≤ 1 day: 0          Layman: 0                Public: 0                        Unlimited: 0          Standard: 0
≤ 1 week: 1         Proficient: 3            Restricted: 3                    Easy: 1               Specialized: 4
≤ 1 month: 4        Expert: 6                Confidential: 7                  Moderate: 4           Bespoke: 7
≤ 6 months: 17      Multiple Experts: 8      Strictly Confidential: 11        Difficult: 10         Multiple Bespoke: 9
> 6 months: 19      -                        -                                -                     -
NOTE This likelihood strategy is based on[10] ISO/IEC 18045:2022.

Likelihood – Elapsed Time:
The elapsed time parameter includes the time to identify a vulnerability and to develop and successfully
apply an exploit. This parameter is measured in calendar time.
Likelihood – Specialist Expertise:
Specialist Expertise refers to the level of generic knowledge of the underlying principles, product type or
attack methods (e.g. Internet protocols, Linux operating systems, exploitation techniques).




                                                                ﻿
                                                 © ISO 2025 – All rights reserved
                                                               14

                                  Licensed to Inlab / Simone Fornaciari (s.fornaciari@inlab.srl)
                               ISO Store Order: OP-1037245 license #1/ Downloaded: 2026-03-26
                                  Single user licence only, copying and networking prohibited.
                                             ISO/DIS 24882:2025(en)

                                          Table 6 — Specialist Expertise
Layman:
Unknowledgeable compared to experts or proficient persons, with no relevant expertise.
EXAMPLE 1 Ordinary person using step-by-step descriptions of an attack that is publicly available.
Proficient:
Knowledgeable in that they are familiar with the security behaviour of the system of interest.
EXAMPLE 2 Experienced owner, ordinary technician knowing simple and popular attacks like odometer tuning, in-
stallation of counterfeit parts.
Expert:
Familiar with the underlying algorithms, protocols, hardware, structures, security behaviour, principles and concepts
of security employed, techniques and tools for the definition of new attacks, cryptography, classical attacks for the
product type, attack methods, etc. implemented in the system of interest.
EXAMPLE 3 Experienced technician or engineer.
Multiple experts:
Different fields of expertise are required at an expert level for distinct steps of an attack.
EXAMPLE 4 Multiple highly experienced engineers who have expertise in different fields (e.g. machine architecture,
communication protocols, feature control logic, software architecture), and which are required at an expert level
for distinct steps of an attack. Special Cybersecurity expertise includes for example state-of-the-art attacks such as
side-channels, cryptoanalysis, 0-day exploits.

Likelihood – Knowledge of System of Interest:
The knowledge of the system of interest is related to the amount of information the attacker is able to
acquire about the system.

                               Table 7 — Knowledge of the System of Interest
Public information:

Next, calculate the Likelihood Value by using this formula:
Likelihood Value = Elapsed Time Value + Specialist Expertise Value + Knowledge of System of Interest Value
+ Window of Opportunity Value + Equipment Value.

≥ 25                                                                Very low

The work products of clause 5.6 shall include:
— [WP-5.6-01] List of likelihood rating for each threat scenario.

The manufacturer shall determine the risk rating for each combination of damage scenario and threat
scenario. The risk rating is based on the impact rating and the likelihood rating.

Determine the risk level by looking up the risk value for the likelihood rating and the impact rating using

6 Cybersecurity technical requirements for risk mitigation

The purpose of this clause is to define technical requirements for mitigating cybersecurity risks. These
requirements establish the necessary security properties for ensuring the integrity, authenticity,
confidentiality, and availability of software and system components. Verification criteria are provided to
enable objective assessment and ensure proper implementation.
The manufacturer shall identify and document appropriate technical solutions that fulfil the specified
requirements (e.g. [WP-5.9-01]).
NOTE 1     The applicability of the technical requirements in this clause can be determined based on risk assessment
unless otherwise mentioned in the applicability clauses of clause 6.

NOTE 2    The term software in this document includes application software, firmware, boot code, etc.
Based on risk assessment.

The system of interest shall verify the authenticity and integrity of a software update.

The system of interest shall provide a method to determine the software version that is installed.
If automatic software updates are available, then the user shall be given the configuration option to opt out
of the automatic software updates.
If automatic software updates are available, then the user shall be given the ability to temporarily postpone
the automatic software update.
Where technically feasible, software updates to fix security issues shall be provided separate from functional
software updates.

This requirement ensures that the system of interest can quickly be securely updated in response to
vulnerabilities, minimizing the scalability risk throughout its lifecycle.

Ensuring the cybersecurity of system of interest involves implementing a secure and reliable update
mechanism. This clause outlines the best practices for designing such a function.
Before initiating any software update, it is important to authenticate servers delivering the updates. This
involves verifying the identity of these servers to confirm that updates are sourced from legitimate and
trusted entities.
The system of interest design should utilize digital signatures to guarantees the integrity and authenticity
of software images. Each update should be signed, and the system of interest should be equipped to verify
these signatures using public keys. This practice ensures that only trusted and untampered updates are
installed.
Incorporate a version control mechanism to prevent the installation of outdated or duplicate software
updates. This prevents regression to previous software versions that may have vulnerabilities.
Implement a rollback mechanism to manage update failures. This allows system of interest to revert to a
prior, stable version if an update does not complete successfully, ensuring minimal disruption to operations
and maintaining system stability.
Design the update function to support resumable downloads, allowing updates to continue seamlessly after
network interruptions. This capability can help in preventing incomplete installations due to connectivity issues.

Confirm the system of interest includes a mechanism to verify the authenticity and integrity of software
updates.
Verify the system of interest correctly executes a valid software update, where both the software and its
signature or other authenticator are valid.
Verify the installed software version is available from the system of interest.
Verify the system of interest detects and prevents the execution of an altered software update.
Verify the system of interest detects and prevents the execution of a software update with an invalid
signature or other authenticator.

The manufacturer shall be able to notify the user that a security update is available.
This requirement ensures that users are aware that an update is available.

Effective communication with users regarding software updates is important for maintaining the security
of machinery.
Notify users when new security updates are available, especially in cases where automatic updates have
been disabled or postponed (e.g. pop-up alerts, email notifications, or dashboard alerts).
Notification should include detailed information about the update's significance, highlighting its important
role in enhancing cybersecurity. Clearly communicate the potential impact on security and operational
performance if updates are delayed or ignored. By underscoring the importance, users are more likely to
understand the necessity of timely updates.
If updates are postponed, set recurring reminders or automatic reactivation of updates after the
postponement period expires.
Confirm that a mechanism to notify users is in place when a security update is available.

attributes.clauseTitle: Secure software - integrity and authenticity check

attributes.clauseText: Based on risk assessment.

The system of interest shall implement mechanisms to verify the integrity and authenticity of the software
components.

Ensure that the software that is executed on the system of interest has not been tampered and is from a
trusted source.

Those mechanisms can include, but are not limited to:
— Secure boot mechanism, an integrity check to protect machinery from unauthorized software execution;
— Periodical checks performed on the software integrity during runtime.
Those mechanisms usually rely on chain of trust models, for example a subsequent sequential verification
of the software components establishing a continuous trust chain, ensuring that only authorized and intact
software is executed. They make use of a security element as trust anchor such as HSM, or others (e.g. TPM,
cryptographic services engine, etc.).
Employ cryptographic algorithms and appropriate key lengths to ensure robust protection against
cryptographic attacks.

The system of interest shall be setup to have a secure by default configuration where security is already
turned on at the time of delivery to be secure.
If the system of interest will allow the configuration to be changed to disable security features, then the

Secure by default configuration ensures robust security without requiring user intervention. This design

The system of interest shall be delivered in a secured state with development features disabled or secured
in production mode.

Production mode ensures that system of interest protection is enabled, and that no unnecessary, unprotected
capabilities are left open or available.

Hardening the design for the production release is important to minimize security risks, prevent
unauthorized access, and to limit attack surfaces. This hardening includes, but is not limited to, the following
measures:
— Disable or strongly protect development features such as test modes, and debug interfaces (e.g. protocols
  like XCP & SSH) before the final product is released to prevent unauthorized access or exposure of
  sensitive information. Examples of strong authentication includes cryptographic based authentication;
— Remove debug symbols, comments, and unreachable code from the production software to reduce the
  attack surface;
— Remove, disable or secure unused features, services, ports, or communication protocols that are not
  required for the final product, to reduce the attack surface;
— Confirm that cryptographic artifacts, such as production keys and certificates, are securely generated,
  injected, and protected according to security requirements.

Confirm that debug symbols, comments, and unreachable code are removed from the production software.
Verify that development features and interfaces are either disabled or strongly secured in production mode.

attributes.clauseTitle: Secure logging and reporting - anomaly detection

attributes.clauseText: Based on risk assessment.

The system of interest shall implement monitoring tools that detect and log unexpected or abnormal
behaviours identified by the risk assessment.
Ensures specific risk-related events are detected.

Ensuring continuous monitoring and detection of unexpected or abnormal behaviours enhances the security
of the system of interest and helps identify potential threats. This includes, but is not limited to:
— Monitoring and logging abnormal resource usage patterns, like sudden spikes in CPU, memory, or
  network usage, that can signal a potential security incident;
— Capturing security event details, including timestamps, identities (e.g. user, component), event types (e.g.
  resource spike, abnormal operation), occurrence counts, and results (e.g. success, failure) if applicable;
— Adding anomaly detection rules based on the system of interest’s operational context, considering
  factors like operational mode and diagnostic modes (e.g. a machine behaving erratically outside normal
  operating hours).

Confirm that the log mechanism includes one or more defined methods for detecting and logging unexpected
or abnormal behaviours.
Verify that any unexpected or abnormal behaviour identified by the risk assessment is detected and logged
correctly.

attributes.clauseTitle: Secure logging and reporting - detection of integrity violations

attributes.clauseText: Based on risk assessment.

The system of interest shall be able to detect and log integrity violation events, such as, but not limited to,
failed digital signature checks, failed secure boot processes, failed message authentication checks.
Ensures that unauthorized modifications or malfunctions due to integrity violation are detected and logged.

Detecting and logging integrity violations enhances security and helps identify potential tampering. This
includes, but is not limited to:
— Logging integrity violations related to software authenticity and execution, such as failed digital
  signature verification during secure updates, failed secure boot processes, or detection of unauthorized
  software modifications;
— Logging violations related to data and message integrity, such as failed message authentication checks,
  corruption detected in stored data, or unexpected modifications to configuration files.

Confirm that the system of interest defines specific integrity violation events to be detected and logged and
that these cover relevant integrity violation scenarios.
Verify that any integrity violation event is detected and logged correctly.

— Restricting access to logs;

cybersecurity relevant functionalities or data (e.g. delete operational data).
Failed Attempts to access shall be limited with appropriate mechanism.
Limiting access attempts protects from brute force attack.

Restricting access to cybersecurity relevant functionalities and data (e.g. deleting operational data) supports
secure system operation. This includes, but is not limited to:
— Provide user authentication mechanisms, such as passwords or PINs, with sufficient complexity

attributes.clauseText: Based on risk assessment.

The system of interest shall implement Role-based Access Control to restrict access to system functions
based on user roles (e.g. owner, operator) following the principle of least privilege.

RBAC minimizes the risk of unauthorized access by ensuring that users can only access the functionalities
required for their role.
principle of least privilege ensures that users and processes do not have unnecessary access, reducing

attributes.clauseTitle: Cybersecurity resilience - denial of service protection

attributes.clauseText: Based on risk assessment.

The system of interest shall implement mechanisms to mitigate the effect of denial of service attacks to its
external network interfaces.
Prevent DOS attack to cause permanent disruption in network operation.

Confirm that the system of interest implements mechanisms to mitigate the effect of DOS attacks to its

The system of interest shall implement mechanism to not harm the external network resources causing
degradation or disruption of services provided by other devices or networks.
Prevent an attacker to exploit the system of interest to perform malicious attacks on the external network.

For components interfacing with external networks, especially those responsible for routing traffic from
internal components, measures to prevent harm to external resources or services needs to be evaluated.
Malicious traffic may originate from a compromised internal component or from the network-facing

A defence in depth approach uses multiple, redundant, diverse layers to ensure that if one layer fails,
subsequent layers will mitigate the risk, enhancing overall resilience against threats.

The defence in depth layered strategy increases the system’s resilience by reducing the likelihood that a
single vulnerability or failure will lead to compromise or major impact.
Each layer needs to be designed with independence in mind, so that the compromise of one does not
invalidate others and with the target to limit the actions of an attacker. Defence in depth is not only about
redundancy, but also diversity in controls and strategies, addressing both technical and operational aspects
of system security.
Defence in depth can include, but is not limited to:
— Implementing preventive measures to reduce the attack surface and block threats before they materialize
  (e.g. access controls, segmentation, cryptography);
— Implementing detection mechanisms to identify ongoing or attempted attacks (e.g. access monitoring,
  anomaly detection, intrusion detection systems);
— Implementing resilience and recovery mechanisms to maintain or restore functionality in the event of an
  incident (e.g. protection, recovery, and secure update mechanisms to mitigate impacts of incidents).

Confirm that the system of interest has been designed with consideration for a defence in depth strategy,
including the use of multiple, independent, and diverse security mechanisms to mitigate cybersecurity risks.

This requirement applies wherever cryptographic mechanisms are used to fulfil other cybersecurity
requirements (e.g. for ensuring confidentiality, integrity, authentication, or secure updates).
The manufacturer shall apply best practices when using cryptography to fulfil cybersecurity requirements.

The effectiveness of cryptography relies on the use of standardized and widely accepted algorithms that
have been peer-reviewed and validated. Following cryptographic best practices, including the application of
recommended key lengths, reduces the risk of vulnerabilities and helps maintain resilience against evolving
threats.

7 Product Lifecycle

Product cybersecurity is central in all phases of the product lifecycle to ensure the security and integrity of
the product, its data, and its users. Below are the phases of the product lifecycle along with details on how
cybersecurity should be addressed.

The manufacturer shall perform a risk assessment per clause 5, create a risk report [WP-5.8-01], and create
a cybersecurity requirements specification [WP-5.9-01] during the design phase per clauses 5.8 and 5.9.
If the design changes during development, then the risk assessment, risk report [WP-5.8-01] and
cybersecurity requirements specification [WP-5.9-01] shall be updated if necessary for the system of
interest that changed.

Implement the cybersecurity requirements specification [WP-5.9-01] defined in the design phase.
During the implementation phase, the manufacturer should ensure that all software development activities
comply with the manufacturer’s secure coding guidelines. The coding guidelines can be referenced by the
cybersecurity requirements specification.

Functional testing shall be performed to verify that the cybersecurity requirements specification [WP-5.9-
01] security measures have been implemented.
The verification criteria shall include the defined verification methods from clause 6 for the selected
technical solutions.

The verification of the implementation may be achieved using different functional testing methods.
The following are examples of such functional testing methods:
— Static code analysis;
— Fuzz testing;
— Unit testing;
— Code reviews.
Testing may be documented in the form of a test procedure. A test procedure can include but is not limited to:
— Objective definition (what should be achieved with the test);
— Test methodology (what kind of tests should be carried out);
— Acceptance criteria (what conditions must be met for the test to be considered passed);
— Test protocols (schemes for documenting the test results).
A verification test report [WP-7.2-01] shall be created to document the results of the testing.

In the validation phase, the manufacturer shall review the overall product to confirm that the risk assessment
and security goals were met.
For products that include off-the-shelf and open-source components, the overall product validation may
include work products [WP-7.2-02] and [WP-7.2-03] related to clauses 9.3 and 9.4.
The manufacturer shall create a validation report [WP-7.2-02] to document the results of the validation review.
The validation and verification reports may be combined in a single document.
Additional testing can be performed to evaluate the effectiveness of the product security such as penetration
testing, fuzz testing, etc. This testing can help to identify threats that were not considered during the
risk assessment. If new threats are identified, then the risk assessment, risk report [WP-5.8-01], and
cybersecurity requirements specification [WP-5.9-01] shall be updated to include the new threats.

The manufacturer shall perform a conformity assessment to make sure all processes were performed
correctly, and the requirements derived in the risk assessment were addressed.
The manufacturer shall create a conformity assessment report [WP-7.2-03] to document the assessment
results.

The production phase is the period while the product is in the manufacturing facility.
The manufacturer shall support production steps that are required to realize the security features of
the product (e.g. enable security by default configuration, injecting of certificates, disable development
interfaces, reference production mode in clause 6.6).
The manufacturer shall install the latest released product software including any security updates that are
available.

The manufacturer shall create a production plan [WP-7.3-01] that includes activities to meet the
cybersecurity requirements.
NOTE      These cybersecurity activities can be added to an existing production plan.

The manufacturer shall conduct a review to confirm that the production plan was implemented. A production
validation report [WP-7.3-02] shall be created to document the results of the review.

The operation phase is from the time the product is delivered from the manufacturing facility until
decommissioning the product at the end of its life.
The operating phase can be viewed as two phases of operation including:
— Operation Phase 1 – Manufacturing delivery to end of cybersecurity support period;
— Operation Phase 2 – end of cybersecurity support to product decommissioning (end of life).
The manufacturer shall define the cybersecurity support period for the user with a cybersecurity support
period plan [WP-7.4-01].
The manufacturer shall define a method for notifying the user that the product has reached the end of the
cybersecurity support period with a cybersecurity support period expiration notification plan [WP-7.4-02].
NOTE      The cybersecurity support period can be subject to local regulations.

The manufacturer shall monitor for events and handle the vulnerabilities as defined in clause 8 during
operation phase 1.
The manufacturer may monitor for events and handle the vulnerabilities as defined in clause 8 during
operation phase 2.

Decommissioning phase refers to the process of systematic retirement and permanent shutdown of a
product.
The manufacturer shall include handling of cybersecurity in the product decommissioning phase.
The manufacturer shall minimally provide a procedure to allow the user to delete their data, cryptographic
material, and settings from the product [WP-7.5-01]. (e.g. reset the product back to default factory settings).
The manufacturer may also provide a procedure to securely transfer the user’s data from one product to
another [WP-7.5-02] (e.g. direct transfer from device to device via Bluetooth or indirect transfer from
device to device via cloud transfer).

8 Vulnerability requirements

Vulnerabilities shall be monitored, analysed, and handled by the manufacturer.
The product shall be free of known exploitable vulnerabilities at market introduction. The identification and
remediation of vulnerabilities should start in the implementation phase.

The manufacturer shall select and document the sources for vulnerability information.
The manufacturer shall perform monitoring for vulnerabilities which should include:
— Continuously review of threat reports for software and hardware bill of materials;

— Scanning of software for known vulnerabilities;
— Monitoring of hardware components for known vulnerabilities;
— Review of potential vulnerability reports that are received from external or internal entities;
— Review of logs and intrusion data from products and its system of interest.
The manufacturer shall create a vulnerability monitoring plan [WP-8.3-01] document which includes:
— Documentation of sources used for vulnerability monitoring;
— Organisational responsibilities;
— Instructions for reporting of vulnerabilities (e.g. external, internal).
NOTE 1     The monitoring actions can detect items that are events, vulnerabilities, or incidents.

NOTE 2     External entities can include supplier feedback, independent researcher feedback, etc.

NOTE 3     The creation of the bill of materials and review of the vulnerabilities can be started in the implementation
phase to expedite discovery and mitigations of vulnerabilities.

The manufacturer shall provide a method for external or internal entities to report potential vulnerabilities
for a product.
The manufacturer’s monitoring activities shall provide a list of events, vulnerabilities, or incidents to be
analysed [WP-8.3-02].
The manufacturer shall conduct a review to confirm that vulnerability monitoring has been implemented.
The manufacturer shall create a vulnerability monitoring validation report [WP-8.3-03] to document and
declare that the vulnerability monitoring plan is established.

The manufacturer shall analyse the list of events, vulnerabilities, or incidents [WP-8.3-02] to determine if
there is impact on the product. The risk assessment process shall be updated to assess the risk rating to the
product (reference clause 5).
The manufacturer’s analysis activities shall provide a list of events, vulnerabilities, or incidents with risk
rating [WP-8.4-01].
Any untreated vulnerabilities should be added to the risk report [WP-5.8-01] to have a complete list of the
product risks.
NOTE       Actively known exploited vulnerabilities can be analysed with higher priority.

The manufacturer shall create a vulnerability handling process document [WP-8.5-01].
The vulnerability handling process shall result in having no unreasonable risks remaining open.
This process shall include:
— Determination of vulnerability risk treatment (reference clause 5.8);
— Vulnerability communications plan [WP-8.6-02];
— Execution timing plan.
NOTE       Actively known exploited vulnerabilities can be handled with higher priority.

The risk assessment shall be updated if the threat landscape has changed.

The risk assessment shall be updated if the product design changes during the vulnerability handling.
The manufacturer’s handling process shall provide documentation evidence [WP-8.5-02] that the
manufacturer handled the vulnerability which can include:
— Product update solution;
— Vulnerability documentation;
— Update notifications.
The manufacturer shall conduct a review to confirm that the vulnerability handling process has been
implemented. A Vulnerability handling validation report [WP-8.5-03] shall be created to document and
declare that the vulnerability handling process is established.

The manufacturer shall create and enforce a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy [WP-8.6-01].
The manufacturer shall make their coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy available to the user.
The manufacturer shall disclose information about resolved vulnerabilities including a description of the
vulnerability, the impacts of the vulnerability, and steps to remediate the vulnerabilities to the user using a
vulnerability communications plan [WP-8.6-02].
The manufacturer may delay providing certain details of the vulnerability to protect the product.
The manufacturer or third-party component supplier shall coordinate the disclosure of vulnerabilities for
components that are used within the product.

When integrating components from third-party sources, it is necessary to ensure all integrations do not
compromise the security of the product and newly discovered vulnerabilities must be managed throughout
the entire product lifecycle.

    ensuring alignment with the intended security objectives of the final system.
attributes.clauseTitle: Requirements for the integration of off-the-shelf components

attributes.clauseText:
When integrating open-source components, manufacturers shall verify that those components do not
compromise the cybersecurity of the product through a thorough investigation of each open-source
component.
Activities carried out to verify the security level of an open-source component can include but are not limited to:
— Verifying that the open-source component receives regular security updates and is still actively
  maintained;
— Checking the open-source component against available vulnerability databases for instances of publicly
  known exploitable vulnerabilities;
— Verifying that the integration of the open-source component into the target system of interest does not
  create a new vulnerability;

                Example of cybersecurity goals and requirements


Security goals and requirements are defined for the controls that mitigate a given risk. The following list
provides examples of security goals and requirements to help illustrate the difference.
a)   Goal - Protect sensitive data
     1) Requirement - Implement end-to-end encryption(s) for all sensitive data stored on agricultural
        machinery systems and transmitted between devices.
     2) Requirement - Utilize secure access controls to restrict data access to authorized personnel only,
        employing multi-factor authentication (MFA).
b) Goal - Ensure system integrity
     1) Requirement - Deploy integrity monitoring tools to detect unauthorized changes to system software
        and configurations.
     2) Requirement - Establish a regular patch management process to ensure that all system components
        and software are up to date with the latest security patches.
c)   Goal - Enhance network security
     1) Requirement - Implement firewalls and intrusion detection system (IDS) and intrusion prevention
        systems (IPS) to protect communication networks associated with machinery.
     2) Requirement - Use virtual private networks (VPNs) for remote access to ensure secure and
        encrypted communications.
d) Goal - Improve incident response and recovery
     1) Requirement - Develop and maintain an incident response plan that includes procedures for
        detecting, reporting, and responding to cybersecurity incidents.
     2) Requirement - Conduct regular incident response, disaster recovery, and business continuity
        planning exercises to ensure rapid recovery from potential cybersecurity incidents.
e)   Goal - Maintain operational availability
     1) Requirement - Implement redundant systems and failover mechanisms to ensure continued
        operation of critical machinery functions during a cybersecurity event.
     2) Requirement - Utilize real-time monitoring systems to detect and respond to anomalies in
        machinery operation.
f)   Goal - Foster security awareness and training
     1) Requirement - Develop comprehensive security awareness training programs for all employees
        handling or operating machinery.

     2) Requirement - Conduct regular phishing simulations and security drills to reinforce training and
        prepare staff for potential threats.
g) Goal - Secure supply chain
     1) Requirement - Conduct thorough security assessments of all third-party vendors and partners to
        ensure compliance with security standards.
     2) Requirement - Incorporate security clauses in contracts with suppliers to mandate adherence to
        cybersecurity practices.
h) Goal - Enhance software development security
     1) Requirement - Integrate security into the software development lifecycle by adopting secure coding

     2) Requirement - Implement automated security testing tools to identify vulnerabilities during the

     1) Requirement - Implement physical tamper detection measures such as electronic module access

78 Installation Instructions
attributes.clauseTitle: Equipment that is not provided with ground-fault protection as specified in the Exception to 75.6.2

attributes.clauseText:
ground fault relay or its functions intended for protection of a solidly grounded wye service rated more than
150 volts to ground and not exceeding 600 volts phase-to-phase shall be provided with information sheets
describing system testing instructions, and with a test form. The form shall include a space for the date
the test was performed and the results, and shall state that the form should be retained by those in charge
of the building’s electrical installation in order to be available to the authority having jurisdiction. The
instructions shall include the following items and shall basically prescribe only that information necessary
to perform the tests. The instructions shall be separate and apart from any more elaborate test detail that
the manufacturer wishes to provide. The instructions shall specify that:

        a) The interconnected system shall be investigated in accordance with the panel
        manufacturer’s detailed instructions, and that this investigation is to be undertaken by qualified
        personnel.

        b) The location of the sensors around the bus of the circuit to be protected shall be determined.
        This can be done visually with knowledge of which bus is involved.

        c) The grounding points of the system shall be verified to determine that ground paths do not
        exist that would bypass the sensors. The use of high-voltage testers and resistance bridges is
        able to be suggested.

        d) The installed system is to be tested for correct response by the application of full scale
        current into the equipment to duplicate a ground-fault condition, or by equivalent means such as
        by a simulated fault current generated by:

                1) A coil around the sensors; or

                2) A separate test winding in the sensors.

        e) The results of the test shall be recorded on the test form provided with the instructions.

                                                                                   I rischi associati ai pericoli relativi all’equipaggiamento elettrico devono essere considerati
                                                                                   come parte delle prescrizioni globali per la valutazione dei rischi della macchina. Questo
                                                                                   permette di stabilire un livello adeguato di riduzione del rischio, e le misure di protezione
                                                                                   necessarie per le persone che possono essere esposte a tali pericoli, pur mantenendo un
                                                                                   livello accettabile di prestazioni della macchina e del suo equipaggiamento.

                                                                                   Le situazioni pericolose possono derivare dalle seguenti cause, ma non sono limitate a esse:

                                                                                   –     guasti o avarie all’equipaggiamento elettrico che determinano la possibilità di scosse
                                                                                         elettriche o di fiamme di origine elettrica;
                                                                                   –     guasti o avarie in circuiti di comando (o componenti e dispositivi associati a tali circuiti)
                                                                                         che provocano un malfunzionamento della macchina;
                                                                                   –     disturbi o interruzioni nelle sorgenti di alimentazione, nonché guasti o avarie nei circuiti di
                                                                                         potenza, che provocano un malfunzionamento della macchina;
                                                                                   –     perdita di continuità dei circuiti, dovuta a contatti striscianti o rotanti, che provoca un
                                                                                         guasto in una funzione di sicurezza;
                                                                                   –     disturbi elettrici, per esempio elettromagnetici, elettrostatici, provenienti dall’esterno o
                                                                                         generati all’interno dell’equipaggiamento elettrico, che provocano un malfunzionamento
                                                                                         della macchina;
                                                                                   –     rilascio di energia (elettrica o meccanica) accumulata che provoca, per esempio, scosse
                                                                                         elettriche o movime

attributes.clauseText:
It is recommended that, where practicable, the electrical equipment of a machine is
                                                                                   connected to a single incoming supply. Where another supply is necessary for certain parts
                                                                                   of the equipment (for example, electronic equipment that operates at a different voltage), that
                                                                                   supply should be derived, as far as is practicable, from devices (for example, transformers,
                                                                                   converters) forming part of the electrical equipment of the machine. For large complex
                                                                                   machinery comprising a number of widely-spaced machines working together in a co-
                                                                                   ordinated manner, there can be a need for more than one incoming supply depending upon
                                                                                   the site supply arrangements (see 5.3.1).

                                                                                   Unless a plug is provided with the machine for the connection to the supply (see 5.3.2 e)), it
                                                                                   is recommended that the supply conductors are terminated at the supply disconnecting
                                                                                   device.

                                                                                   Where a neutral conductor is used it shall be clearly indicated in the technical documentation
                                                                                   of the machine, such as in the installation diagram and in the circuit diagram, and a separate
                                                                                   insulated terminal, labelled N in accordance with 16.1, shall be provided for the neutral
                                                                                   conductor (see also Annex B).

                                                                                   There shall be no connection between the neutral conductor and the protective bonding
                                                                                   circuit inside the electrical equipment nor shall a combined PEN terminal be provided.

                                                                                   Exception: a connection may be made between the neutral terminal and the PE terminal at
                                                                                   the point of the connection of the power supply to the machine for TN-C systems.




                                                                                    NORMA TECNICA

attributes.clauseText:
A supply disconnecting device shall be provided:

                                                                                   –    for each incoming source of supply to a machine(s);
                                                                                        NOTE The incoming supply can be connected directly to the machine or via a feeder system. Feeder systems
                                                                                        of machines can include conductor wires, conductor bars, slip-ring assemblies, flexible cable systems (reeled,
                                                                                        festooned) or inductive power supply systems.

                                                                                   –    for each on-board power supply.

                                                                                   The supply disconnecting device shall disconnect (isolate) the electrical equipment of the
                                                                                   machine from the supply when required (for example for work on the machine, including the
                                                                                   electrical equipment).

                                                                                   When two or more supply disconnecting devices are provided, protective interlocks for their
                                                                                   correct operation shall also be provided in order to prevent a hazardous situation, including
                                                                                   damage to the machine or to the work in progress.




                                                                                    NORMA TECNICA
                                                                                    CEI EN 60204-1:2006-09

                                                                                   Tutti i morsetti per il collegamento dell’alimentazione devono essere chiaramente identificati
                                                                                   conformemente alla IEC 60445 e a 16.1. Per l’identificazione del morsetto del conduttore di
                                                                                   protezione esterno, vedere 5.2.

                                                                                   Vedere 17.8 per le disposizioni sulle istruzioni relative alla manutenzione.

attributes.clauseText:
When the supply disconnecting device is one of the types specified in 5.3.2 a) to d) it shall
                                                                                   fulfil all of the following requirements:

                                                                                   –   isolate the electrical equipment from the supply and have one OFF (isolated) and one
                                                                                       ON position marked with "O" and "I" (symbols IEC 60417-5008 (DB:2002-10) and
                                                                                       IEC 60417-5007 (DB:2002-10), see 10.2.2);
                                                                                   –   have a visible contact gap or a position indicator which cannot indicate OFF (isolated)
                                                                                       until all contacts are actually open and the requirements for the isolating function have
                                                                                       been satisfied;
                                                                                   –   have an external operating means (for example handle), (exception: power-operated




Copia concessa a MECQ in data 06/01/2007 da CEI-Comitato Elettrotecnico Italiano
                                                                                       switchgear need not be operable from outside the enclosure where there are other means
                                                                                       to open it). Where the external operating means is not intended for emergency operations,
                                                                                       it is recommended that it be coloured BLACK or GREY (see 10.7.4 and 10.8.4);
                                                                                   –   be provided with a means permitting it to be locked in the OFF (isolated) position (for
                                                                                       example by padlocks). When so locked, remote as well as local closing shall be
                                                                                       prevented;
                                                                                   –   disconnect all live conductors of its power supply circuit. However, for TN supply systems,
                                                                                       the neutral conductor may or may not be disconnected except in countries where
                                                                                       disconnection of the neutral conductor (when used) is compulsory;

                                                                                       loads. The calculated breaking capacity may be reduced by the use of a proven diversity
                                                                                       factor.

                                                                                   –   have the switching capability, or be interlocked with a switching device that has a

attributes.clauseText:
The operating means (for example, a handle) of the supply disconnecting device shall be
                                                                                   easily accessible and located between 0,6 m and 1,9 m above the servicing level. An upper
                                                                                   limit of 1,7 m is recommended.
                                                                                   NOTE The direction of operation is given in IEC 61310-3.
attributes.sourceFile: EN 60204-1- Safety of machinery - Electrical equipment of machines - General requirements.pdf

attributes.clauseText:
The following circuits need not be disconnected by the supply disconnecting device:

                                                                                   –   lighting circuits for lighting needed during maintenance or repair;
                                                                                   –   plug and socket outlets for the exclusive connection of repair or maintenance tools and
                                                                                       equipment (for example hand drills, test equipment);
                                                                                   –   undervoltage protection circuits that are only provided for automatic tripping in the event
                                                                                       of supply failure;
                                                                                   –   circuits supplying equipment that should normally remain energized for correct operation
                                                                                       (for example temperature controlled measuring devices, product (work in progress)
                                                                                       heaters, program storage devices);
                                                                                   –   control circuits for interlocking.

                                                                                   It is recommended, however, that such circuits be provided with their own disconnecting
                                                                                   device.

                                                                                   Where such a circuit is not disconnected by the supply disconnecting device:

                                                                                   –   permanent warning label(s) in accordance with 16.1 shall be appropriately placed in
                                                                                       proximity to the supply disconnecting device;




Copia concessa a MECQ in data 06/01/2007 da CEI-Comitato Elettrotecnico Italiano
                                                                                   –   a corresponding statement shall be included in the maintenance manual, and one or more
                                                                                       of the following shall apply;
                                                                                       –    a permanent warning label in accordance with 16.1 is affixed in proximity to each
                                                                                            excepted circuit, or
                                                                                       –    the excepted circuit is separated from other circuits, or
                                                                                       –    the conductors are identified by colour taking into account the recommendation of
                                                                                            13.2.4.

attributes.clauseText:
Devices for switching off for the prevention of unexpected start-up shall be provided (for
                                                                                   example where, during maintenance, a start-up of the machine or part of the machine can
                                                                                   create a hazard).

                                                                                   Such devices shall be appropriate and convenient for the intended use, shall be suitably
                                                                                   placed, and readily identifiable as to their function and purpose (for example by a durable
                                                                                   marking in accordance with 16.1 where necessary).
                                                                                   NOTE 1 This part of IEC 60204 does not address all provisions for prevention of unexpected start up. See
                                                                                   ISO 14118 (EN 1037).
                                                                                   NOTE 2 Further information on the location and actuation of devices such as those used for the prevention of
                                                                                   unexpected start-up is provided in EN 60447.

                                                                                   Means shall be provided to prevent inadvertent and/or mistaken closure of these devices
                                                                                   either at the controller or from other locations (see also 5.6).
